summary.short: Amends Law No. 5651 on internet publications. For social network providers with over one million daily accesses from Turkey, requires a Turkish representative, reporting, 48-hour replies to applications and local data hosting, enforced by escalating fines, advertising bans and bandwidth throttling. Articles 6-7 apply from 1 October 2020.
summary.long: Amends Law No. 5651 on internet publications. Defines social network providers. Lets administrative fines be notified directly to addressees abroad. Raises a fine under Article 5(6) from 100,000 to 1,000,000 Turkish lira. Adds content removal to access-blocking rules and sets four-hour compliance for Union orders. Additional Article 4 covers social network providers with over one million daily accesses from Turkey: they must appoint a Turkish representative and notify the Authority, answer applications within 48 hours, publish six-monthly reports, and take steps to store Turkish users' data in Turkey. Non-compliance draws administrative fines, a ban on new advertising by Turkish-resident taxpayers, and, on application to a criminal judgeship of peace, bandwidth reduction of up to 90%. Providers are liable for damages if unlawful content identified by a court is not removed within 24 hours of notice. A transitional provision allows three months to prepare for application duties and sets June 2021 for the first report. Articles 6 and 7 apply from 1 October 2020; other provisions from publication.

notes: This is an amending law; its operative provisions change Law 5651 and add a transitional provision. Restated amended wording in Madde 4 and 5 is substitution text and is not coded as new obligations. Kurum, Başkan and Birlik are not defined in this text. Madde 8 sets different commencement: Madde 1 (s) and Madde 6 and 7 take effect 1/10/2020, other provisions on publication. Ek Madde 4(7) states judicial fines in days ('elli bin gün') and doubles administrative fines for repeats within one year.
